Paper: SWE-bench: Can Language Models Resolve Real-World GitHub Issues?
Authors: Carlos E. Jimenez; John Yang; Alexander Wettig; Shunyu Yao; Kexin Pei; Ofir Press; Karthik Narasimhan
Methodology: Issue plus pinned repository snapshot; candidate patch judged by repository tests; BM25 baseline included
Findings: Initial Claude 2 result was 1.96 percent; establishes a public real-issue repair benchmark
Limitations: Release dataset Python-only; initial tested methods intentionally simple; official grading requires benchmark harness
Relevance to DevMind: Benchmark precedent; not a DevMind result

Paper: SWE-agent: Agent-Computer Interfaces Enable Automated Software Engineering
Authors: John Yang; Carlos E. Jimenez; Alexander Wettig; Kilian Lieret; Shunyu Yao; Karthik Narasimhan; Ofir Press
Methodology: Language model plus purpose-built agent-computer interface for navigation, editing, and tests; interface ablations
Findings: 12.47 percent SWE-bench with GPT-4 Turbo; 87.7 percent HumanEvalFix
Limitations: Results are configuration and benchmark dependent; limited tool set and failure modes discussed by authors
Relevance to DevMind: DevMind is not an autonomous tool-using agent

Authors: Yuntong Zhang; Haifeng Ruan; Zhiyu Fan; Abhik Roychoudhury
Methodology: AST-aware iterative code search directed by an LLM; optional spectrum-based fault localization; patch generation
Metrics: Resolution; cost; runtime; manual patch assessment
Findings: 57/300 resolved (19 percent); about USD 0.43 and four minutes per task in reported setup
Limitations: Depends on tests for spectrum-based localization; one benchmark/model setup; manual acceptability assessment has judgment uncertainty
Relevance to DevMind: Prior art for iterative evidence retrieval and repair

Paper: RepairAgent: An Autonomous, LLM-Based Agent for Program Repair
Authors: Islem Bouzenia; Premkumar Devanbu; Michael Pradel
Methodology: Repair tools, dynamically updated prompts, and finite-state control
Metrics: Correct fixes; token use; time; cost
Findings: 164 Defects4J fixes including 39 not fixed by prior techniques; about 270k tokens and USD 0.14 per bug under stated pricing
Limitations: Possible training-data leakage; multi-line/multi-file bugs may receive partial edits
Relevance to DevMind: Prior art for bounded stateful tool workflows

Paper: Agentless: Demystifying LLM-Based Software Engineering Agents
Authors: Chunqiu Steven Xia; Yinlin Deng; Soren Dunn; Lingming Zhang
Research problem: Repository-level software issue repair without an interactive agent
Methodology: Structured localization, repair sampling, regression and generated reproduction test validation
Findings: 96/300 fixes (32 percent), about USD 0.70 per task in reported setup
Limitations: Authors identify issue descriptions with disclosed solutions, insufficient information, or misleading content; model/benchmark dependent
Relevance to DevMind: Prior art for structured stages and evidence/test gates

Paper: Improved IR-based Bug Localization with Intelligent Relevance Feedback (BRaIn)
Methodology: LLM relevance feedback reformulates queries and reranks retrieved source documents
Findings: Conference abstract reports relative improvements of 87.6, 89.5, and 48.8 percent respectively
Limitations: Localization only; metrics depend on dataset/split and do not measure patch resolution
Relevance to DevMind: Direct prior work on query reformulation and semantic relevance feedback
Evidence access: Conference page and preprint abstract inspected

Paper: LLM-BL: Large Language Models are Zero-Shot Rankers for Bug Localization
Authors: Zhengliang Li; Zhiwei Jiang; Qiguo Huang; Qing Gu
Research problem: Project-level bug localization under context limits
Methodology: Report expansion; candidate retrieval; content reduction; listwise LLM ranking
Dataset: Six public Java and Python projects
Metrics: Localization ranking metrics; final paper metrics not yet reconciled
Findings: Abstract reports better results for ChatGPT and Llama 3 than CodeLlama and compared methods without task-specific fine-tuning
Limitations: Localization only; final metric values require inspection of proceedings paper
Relevance to DevMind: Prior art for expanded queries and LLM reranking
Evidence access: Official conference page inspected; proceedings PDF pending

Paper: Reformulate, Retrieve, Localize: Agents for Repository-Level Bug Localization
Methodology: Non-fine-tuned open LLM extracts identifiers/code cues and reformulates before BM25
Findings: Abstract reports 35 percent better first-file ranking than BM25 and up to +22 percent file retrieval over SWE-agent
Limitations: Workshop/preprint; localization only, not repair; comparisons depend on setup
Relevance to DevMind: Direct overlap with deterministic query enrichment concept

Paper: RepoDebug: Repository-Level Multi-Task and Multi-Language Debugging Evaluation of Large Language Models
Authors: Jingjing Liu; Zeming Liu; Zihao Cheng; Mengliang He; Xiaoming Shi; Yuhang Guo; Xiangrong Zhu; Yuanfang Guo; Yunhong Wang; Haifeng Wang
Methodology: AST-based fault injection and repository split; identification, localization, repair tasks
Findings: Ten models evaluated; strongest reported model still has difficulty on repository-level debugging
Limitations: Injected faults differ from historical user reports and maintainer fixes
Relevance to DevMind: Useful benchmark precedent; not direct issue/PR evaluation

Paper: An Empirical Study on the Classification of Bug Reports with Machine Learning
Authors: Renato Andrade; C?sar Teixeira; Nuno Laranjeiro; Marco Vieira
Venue: IEEE Open Journal of the Computer Society, vol. 7, pp. 1213-1224
Research problem: Issue-report classification across projects and issue-tracking systems
Methodology: Compares SVM, Logistic Regression, Random Forest, report title versus description, language/tracker effects, and cross-project generalization
Dataset: More than 660,000 reports from 52 projects, 10 languages, and 3 issue trackers
Findings: SVM, Logistic Regression, and Random Forest perform effectively; title and description do not differ significantly overall; language and tracker affect results
Limitations: Project selection and hyperparameter settings are threats; publisher page and abstract checked, full-text access limited
Relevance to DevMind: Shows supervised bug-report classification is established and requires labelled data
Evidence access: 2026 IEEE publisher metadata/abstract checked; 2025 author preprint inspected

Paper: Learning Software Bug Reports: A Systematic Literature Review
Authors: Guoming Long; Jingzhi Gong; Hui Fang; Tao Chen
Venue: ACM Transactions on Software Engineering and Methodology
Research problem: Map machine-learning research on bug-report analytics
Methodology: Systematic literature review with screening and detailed study selection
Findings: TF-IDF and Word2Vec are common representations; categorization is the most frequent task; many studies lack robust statistical tests
Limitations: Review-level evidence; not a direct DevMind comparison
Relevance to DevMind: Supports conservative novelty and evaluation framing
Evidence access: Publisher record and full manuscript inspected

Paper: Improving IR-based Bug Localization with Semantics-Driven Query Reduction (IQLoc)
Authors: Asif Mohammed Samir; Mohammad Masudur Rahman
Venue: Journal of Systems and Software, vol. 237, article 112860
Research problem: Semantic query reduction for bug localization
Methodology: Transformer relevance reasoning over lexical candidates followed by query reduction and reranking
Dataset: About 7,500 Java bug reports based on Bench4BL plus recent reports
Findings: The arXiv v2 manuscript reports gains across random and time-based splits; version-specific figures are omitted pending journal reconciliation
Limitations: Java-only evaluation; possible label noise; reimplemented baselines; context-size effects not fully studied
Relevance to DevMind: Direct prior art for semantic query reformulation and hybrid retrieval
Evidence access: Full arXiv v2 inspected; journal full-text access blocked

Paper: SWERank: Software Issue Localization with Code Ranking
Authors: Revanth Gangi Reddy; Tarun Suresh; JaeHyeok Doo; Ye Liu; Xuan-Phi Nguyen; Yingbo Zhou; Semih Yavuz; Caiming Xiong; Heng Ji; Shafiq Joty
DOI or arXiv: Official ICLR paper; no DOI identified
Research problem: Learned code ranking for software issue localization
Methodology: Fine-tuned bi-encoder retrieval and listwise LLM reranking
Dataset: SWE-LOC training data; SWE-bench Lite (274 retained); LocBench (560)
Metrics: Acc@k at file, module, and function levels
Findings: Reports stronger localization than evaluated agentic and retrieval baselines
Limitations: Large training data and models up to 32B; localization is not repair resolution
Relevance to DevMind: Retrieval benchmark precedent; beyond the verified local compute budget

Paper: SpIDER: Spatially Informed Dense Embedding Retrieval for Software Issue Localization
Authors: Shravan S. Chaudhari; Rahul Thomas Jacob; Jiajun Cao; Muhammad Shihab Rashid; Mononito Goswami; Christian Bock
Research problem: Graph-aware dense code retrieval for issue localization
Methodology: Dense retrieval seeds followed by syntax/call-graph candidate expansion with traceable reasons
Dataset: SpIDER-Bench from SWEPolyBench, SWE-bench Verified, and Multi-SWE-bench; four languages
Findings: Containment expansion adds +0.05 to +0.12 absolute recall; call-edge exploration adds +0.11 to +0.19 over dense retrieval in reported setups
Limitations: Requires dense models and graph construction; results do not validate DevMind embeddings
Evidence access: Full paper landing page and abstract inspected

Paper: EviACT: An Evidence-to-Action Framework for Agentic Program Repair
Authors: Qianru Meng; Xiao Zhang; Zhaochun Ren; Joost Visser
Research problem: Evidence-guided repository repair with test gates
Methodology: Evidence scaffold, compile/apply gate, target and regression-test gates, bounded retries, and re-localization
Dataset: Defects4J 2.0 (835); SWE-bench Verified (500), Lite (300), and Live (100)
Metrics: Resolution rate; cost; Hit@3; failure categories; manual patch review
Findings: Reports improvements over selected baselines; manual review judged 78/100 resolved patches correct, 12 overfit, and 10 indeterminate
Limitations: Preprint; contamination cannot be ruled out; bounded graph expansion can miss causes; 12 percent of audited resolved patches overfit
Relevance to DevMind: Strong precedent for bounded tests and distinct patch/test status

Paper: RepoAI: Automated code refactoring through multi-agent LLM orchestration and retrieval-augmented generation
Authors: Nacha Chondamrongkul; Moe Pyae Pyae Kyaw; Soe Moe Ko; Pyae Phyo Paing; Min Khant Than Swe; Tew Hongthong
Venue: Science of Computer Programming, vol. 253, article 103477
Methodology: Multi-agent RAG generation and cross-family validation
Dataset: 100 RefactorBench tasks from 10+ projects; 7 generator models; 1,404 reported evaluation cases/runs
Metrics: Friedman and Wilcoxon tests; error taxonomy
Findings: Publisher abstract reports full pipeline beats direct generation (Wilcoxon p=0.007); 170 failures categorized
Limitations: Refactoring is not issue localization or repair; full text unavailable in the scoped review
Relevance to DevMind: Do not call DevMind multi-agent; adjacent RAG orchestration precedent
Evidence access: Publisher metadata and abstract checked; full text returned 403 in original review

Paper: Loc2Repair: A Framework for Evaluating the Impact of File-Level Issue Localization in Repo-Level LLM Repair
Authors: Mohammad Nour Al Awad; Sergey Ivanov
Research problem: Controlled analysis of file localization effects on repair
Methodology: Same repair setup under no-localization, predicted-location, and gold-file conditions
Findings: Preprint reports pooled resolution of 44.7 percent without localization, 48.9-49.1 percent with predicted localization, and 52.4 percent with gold localization
Limitations: Preprint and one benchmark; file-level labels and model/runtime specific
Relevance to DevMind: Direct prior art for localization-to-repair relationship

Paper: Retrieval-Oriented Code Representations in Agentic Bug Localization
Authors: Genevieve Caumartin; Tse-Hsun Chen; Diego Elias Costa
Research problem: Representation, retrieval, ranking, and cost in issue localization
Methodology: Compares paths, raw code, and generated summaries under lexical, semantic, and LLM retrieval/reranking
Findings: Role-aware summaries can improve Hit@5 over path-based representations with smaller footprint; combinations/reranking improve retrieval in reported settings
Limitations: Preprint; file-level results on selected datasets; generated summaries/reranking add inference cost

Paper: When Deep Learning Meets Information Retrieval-based Bug Localization: A Survey
Authors: Feifei Niu; Chuanyi Li; Kui Liu; Xin Xia; David Lo
Research problem: Survey and meta-analysis of deep-learning IR-based bug localization
Methodology: Synthesizes methods and evaluation across 61 IR-based localization studies
Findings: Maps representations, methods, evaluation practices, and open issues
Limitations: Survey context, not a directly comparable system result
Relevance to DevMind: Distinguishes classical lexical IR, learned semantic retrieval, and repair
